{"consolidated_memory":"## Conflict Loop in mobile/ios/SyncEngine.swift — Multiple Incidents

The mobile sync engine in mobile/ios/SyncEngine.swift has experienced a recurring class of conflict loop issues. In each case, two clients rewrite each other on every pass. The standard repro is: edit the same note on two devices while offline. Below are four distinct occasions:

### Occasion 1: Schema Drift Conflict Loop [2026-03-01]
**Trigger:** Appeared only after a rolling restart of the fleet.
**Root cause:** Schema drift between the migration and the model.
**Signal:** Two clients rewriting each other on every pass.
**Outcome:** p99 latency fell from 1.7 s to 127 ms.
**Fix:** Regenerated the model from the migration and pinned the checksum.
**PR #2260, branch fix/conflict-loop-1.**

### Occasion 2: Missing Composite Index Conflict Loop [2026-03-06]
**Trigger:** Only for payloads above roughly two megabytes.
**Root cause:** A missing composite index on (tenant_id, created_at).
**Signal:** Two clients rewriting each other on every pass.
**Outcome:** The nightly rollup matched the source counts for 50 days running.
**Fix:** Added the composite index and backfilled in batches.
**PR #3292, branch fix/conflict-loop-2.**

### Occasion 3: Naive Datetime Conflict Loop [2026-03-10]
**Trigger:** Only for deeply nested inputs beyond six levels.
**Root cause:** A naive datetime compared against an aware one.
**Signal:** Two clients rewriting each other on every pass.
**Outcome:** Cold start dropped 92 percent, to 465 ms.
**Fix:** Made every boundary timezone aware at the edge.
**PR #7136, branch fix/conflict-loop-3.**

### Occasion 4: Clock Skew Conflict Loop [2026-08-11]
**Trigger:** Only for users sitting in a negative UTC offset.
**Root cause:** Clock skew between the two hosts.
**Signal:** Two clients rewriting each other on every pass.
**Outcome:** Reclaimed 34 GB of blob storage.
**Fix:** Switched the deadline to a monotonic clock.
**PR #8959, branch fix/conflict-loop-6.**

**Context:** All four occasions involve the same corner of mobile/ios/SyncEngine.swift on the mobile sync side, so context carried over between fixes."}
